questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose Milan as my study destination because of its strong academic reputation in law, particularly its focus on international and European legal studies, which aligned perfectly with my educational goals.

Additionally, I love the italian culture, offering an environment where I could grow personally and professionally. The opportunity to improve my italian language skills in an immersive setting was another important factor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing can be competitive, so start your search early and consider various options like shared apartments or student residences. Understanding rental contracts and Italian tenancy laws is essential, as is budgeting for utilities, which are often not included in rent. Familiarize yourself with the city’s neighborhoods to choose one that suits your lifestyle and commute to campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy and convenient.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at Statale in Milan was relatively straightforward but required careful attention to deadlines and documentation. Upon arrival, I had to complete the initial registration at the International Office, where they provided guidance on the necessary forms and procedures. This included submitting my learning agreement, proof of enrollment from my home university, a copy of my passport, and health insurance documentation. I also received access to the university’s online platform, where I could register for courses and track my academic progress.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistance from the International Office was invaluable, and we also supported one another as students navigating the same process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I had all the courses I wanted to have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice to future exchange students registering at Statale in Milan is to start early and stay organized. Make sure to carefully read all the emails and instructions from the International Office, as the process involves multiple steps and specific deadlines. Additionally, be proactive in reaching out to the International Office or your program coordinator if you have any doubts—they are usually very responsive and willing to assist. Finally, don’t hesitate to ask for help from fellow students, as they can provide tips and share their own experiences navigating the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic program at Statale in Milan. The courses were well-structured and offered a comprehensive perspective on international and European law, which aligned perfectly with my academic interests. The professors were knowledgeable and often incorporated practical case studies, making the learning experience engaging and relevant.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at Statale were generally well-structured and provided a solid foundation in international and European law. While the level of difficulty varied, most courses were accessible and offered a good mix of theoretical knowledge and practical application. Some courses were more introductory, which was great for broadening my understanding of specific areas, while others were a bit more advanced, involving detailed readings and case discussions. The professors were supportive and encouraged critical thinking, but the pace of some courses was manageable. While the academic program wasn't overly demanding, it still allowed me to gain valuable insights into the subjects I studied, and I felt that the learning experience was both informative and practical.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at Statale in Milan was quite different from that at UCPH. While there were lectures, there was little emphasis on self-study or homework. Most of the learning occurred during the lectures, and the focus was more on listening to the professor rather than engaging in group work or completing assignments outside of class. In contrast, at UCPH, there is a much stronger focus on active participation, group discussions, and independent study, with a higher expectation of homework and self-directed learning. At Statale, the workload was lighter, and I found the academic environment to be more relaxed with less pressure for ongoing assignments and more freedom during the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was fairly satisfied with the non-academic opportunities at Statale. While the university offers a variety of student clubs and extracurricular activities, I found that the options were somewhat limited compared to what I expected. However, there were still opportunities to get involved in cultural events and activities, especially through student organizations. Milan itself provided a wealth of non-academic experiences, from sports facilities to social events, which made up for the fewer on-campus opportunities. I also had the chance to attend events organized by the university’s international office, which helped me connect with other exchange students and locals.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was possible to be part of several student groups where you could socialize with other students. For example, there was an Erasmus Group that provided for several social events every week which was very nice!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To join every beer pong/wine bar event to socialize with other students. Also, to join on trips that are arranged, such as the trip to Germany and the ski trip!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
To go on day trips to other parts of Italy.

I highly recommend visiting a mix of local and nearby destinations during weekends and holidays. 

In Milan, take time to explore the different districts. 

For a peaceful getaway, head to Lake Como for stunning views and charming towns, or visit Verona to see Juliet’s balcony and immerse yourself in the city’s rich history. Lake Garda, Venice, Florence, Turin and other cities are also beautiful.

Lastly, be sure to check out student events and local markets, as they offer great opportunities to connect with others and experience Milanese life.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One of the main differences was the pace of life. In Italy, especially in Milan, everything tends to be more relaxed and unhurried, which was a shift from the more efficient, time-conscious culture I was used to in Norway. This difference extended to daily life, such as dining habits—meals in Italy are often longer and more social, with a strong emphasis on enjoying the moment, while in Norway, meals tend to be quicker. Another cultural adjustment was communication style. Italians tend to be more expressive and spontaneous, with lively conversations and frequent use of gestures, whereas Norwegians are more reserved and tend to value quiet, direct communication. Lastly, while I appreciated the warmth of Italian hospitality, I had to adjust to the more informal and sometimes chaotic approach to organization, which is quite different from Norway’s more structured and orderly way of doing things.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
There are so many aspects of Italian culture that I truly appreciated during my time in Milan. One of the highlights was the strong sense of community and family. Italians place a lot of value on spending time with loved ones, and it was inspiring to see how meals, celebrations, and even everyday moments are often shared with family and friends. I also really enjoyed the Italian approach to food

The Italian sense of style, both in fashion and architecture, also stood out to me. Milan, being a fashion capital, is full of creative energy, and the city’s beautiful historical landmarks and design-oriented spaces reflect a deep appreciation for aesthetics. Finally, the Italian attitude toward life—embracing the present, enjoying the little things, and maintaining a strong connection to culture and history—was something I found truly inspiring and enriching.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Embrace the relaxed pace of life: The atmosphere in Milan is much more laid-back compared to the more time-structured environment at UCPH. Don’t be surprised if things move slower than you’re used to, especially when it comes to meals, socializing, and even certain administrative processes. Take this as an opportunity to slow down, enjoy the moment, and embrace the Italian way of life.

Prepare for less structured academic life: Unlike UCPH, where there’s a strong emphasis on participation, homework, and group work, Statale’s academic approach is more lecture-focused with fewer assignments or interactive classes. You’ll have more flexibility with your time, but it’s important to stay disciplined and keep up with the reading and exams on your own.

Explore Milan and Italy: Milan is a fantastic base for weekend trips, whether it’s to explore nearby cities like Verona or Lake Como or diving deeper into the cultural treasures within the city itself. Don’t just stay on campus—take the opportunity to immerse yourself in Italian culture, try new foods, visit museums, and travel as much as possible. The city has so much to offer, and it’s an experience you won’t want to miss.
